# British spellings that XML documentation must not use, and their US English forms.
#
# CLAUDE.md requires XML documentation in US English. `python3 bld/check-docs.py spelling` reports each word below
# found, whole and in any case, in the prose of a /// comment under a project's src/, test/ or shared/ folder, with
# the US form to write instead. Code blocks, inline code, tag attributes and URLs are not read, and generated files
# are skipped. A line that must keep a British spelling (a name, or text quoted from a third party) goes in
# us-spelling-allowlist.txt with its reason.
#
# Format: one `british -> american` pair per line, every inflection on a line of its own; `#` starts a comment.
#
# Deliberately not listed: "Mondayisation" and its inflections, New Zealand's legal term for moving a holiday off a
# weekend, which the calendar fixtures also use as a policy id; and "labour", above.

# The -ise verbs and their inflections (-ize in US English). The list is explicit: words such as otherwise,
# precise, exercise, promise, noise, advise, devise, comprise, compromise, surprise, expertise, enterprise,
# premise, revise and supervise are spelled the same in US English, so no ending alone flags a word.
amortise -> amortize
amortises -> amortizes
amortised -> amortized
amortising -> amortizing
amortisation -> amortization
authorise -> authorize
authorises -> authorizes
authorised -> authorized
authorising -> authorizing
authorisation -> authorization
authorisations -> authorizations
canonicalise -> canonicalize
canonicalises -> canonicalizes

canonicalisation -> canonicalization

# analyse (analyze). Not "analyses", which is also the plural of analysis.
analyse -> analyze
analysed -> analyzed
analysing -> analyzing
analyser -> analyzer
analysers -> analyzers

# The -our nouns (-or). "Labour" is left out: the calendar data names Labour Day, a holiday's own name.
behaviour -> behavior
behaviours -> behaviors
behavioural -> behavioral
behaviourally -> behaviorally
colour -> color
colours -> colors
coloured -> colored
colouring -> coloring
colourful -> colorful
colourless -> colorless
endeavour -> endeavor
endeavours -> endeavors
endeavoured -> endeavored
endeavouring -> endeavoring
favour -> favor
favours -> favors
favoured -> favored
favouring -> favoring
favourable -> favorable
favourably -> favorably
favourite -> favorite
favourites -> favorites
flavour -> flavor
flavours -> flavors
flavoured -> flavored
flavouring -> flavoring
flavourless -> flavorless
honour -> honor
honours -> honors
honoured -> honored
honouring -> honoring
honourable -> honorable
neighbour -> neighbor
neighbours -> neighbors
neighbouring -> neighboring
neighbourhood -> neighborhood
neighbourhoods -> neighborhoods
rigour -> rigor
unfavourable -> unfavorable
dishonour -> dishonor
misbehaviour -> misbehavior

# The doubled l before an ending on an unstressed syllable (single in US English). "Cancellation" keeps its
# double l in US English too, and "canceled" is how the BCL spells it (IsCanceled, TaskCanceledException).
labelled -> labeled
labelling -> labeling
relabelled -> relabeled
relabelling -> relabeling
unlabelled -> unlabeled
modelled -> modeled
modelling -> modeling
modeller -> modeler
modellers -> modelers
unmodelled -> unmodeled
remodelled -> remodeled
remodelling -> remodeling
cancelled -> canceled
cancelling -> canceling
cancellable -> cancelable
uncancelled -> uncanceled
travelled -> traveled
travelling -> traveling
traveller -> traveler
travellers -> travelers
signalled -> signaled
signalling -> signaling
levelled -> leveled
levelling -> leveling
totalled -> totaled
totalling -> totaling
funnelled -> funneled
funnelling -> funneling
marshalled -> marshaled
marshalling -> marshaling
unmarshalled -> unmarshaled
unmarshalling -> unmarshaling
channelled -> channeled
channelling -> channeling
tunnelled -> tunneled
tunnelling -> tunneling
fuelled -> fueled
fuelling -> fueling
equalled -> equaled
equalling -> equaling
dialled -> dialed
dialling -> dialing

# The -re nouns (-er).
centre -> center
centres -> centers
centred -> centered
centring -> centering
metre -> meter
metres -> meters
millimetre -> millimeter
millimetres -> millimeters
centimetre -> centimeter
centimetres -> centimeters
kilometre -> kilometer
kilometres -> kilometers

# The -ogue nouns (-og). Prologue and epilogue are spelled the same in US English.
catalogue -> catalog
catalogues -> catalogs
catalogued -> cataloged
cataloguing -> cataloging
analogue -> analog
analogues -> analogs

# The -ence nouns (-ense). "Licence" is the British noun; the US noun and verb are both "license".
licence -> license
licences -> licenses
defence -> defense
defences -> defenses
offence -> offense
offences -> offenses
pretence -> pretense

# Other spellings.
acknowledgement -> acknowledgment
acknowledgements -> acknowledgments
artefact -> artifact
artefacts -> artifacts
enrol -> enroll
enrols -> enrolls
enrolment -> enrollment
enrolments -> enrollments
fulfil -> fulfill
fulfils -> fulfills
fulfilment -> fulfillment
grey -> gray
greys -> grays
greyed -> grayed
greying -> graying
greyscale -> grayscale
judgement -> judgment
judgements -> judgments
misspelt -> misspelled
programme -> program
programmes -> programs
whilst -> while
